entries.name: Aurochs
entries.aliases: Aurochs is singular and plural in the source context. Use its separate awakened player trait block. Cattle has its own package.

source.name: Aurochs
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Aurochs Traits
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
sourceDistinctions: The printed conversion is Medium and has its own page-82 traits, separate from Cattle. Charge works on the Strength-based gore in this build because it is a melee weapon attack even though an unarmed strike is not a weapon.

entries.name: Awakened Shrub
entries.aliases: Awakened Shrub / Awakened Shrubs. Use its dedicated player trait block. Awakened Tree and other plant folk are separate.

source.name: Awakened Shrub
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition. The rules below use the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: Kamstra prints a usable trait block and describes the option as very weak in the play advice and design notes. Tanglebud uses the printed values.
The trait block has no No Hands line. Tanglebud fights without weapons, shields, or any item that must be manipulated.
The supplement’s p. 7 rule limits Martial Arts bonus strikes to the class damage die and bludgeoning damage. Tanglebud’s Attack action can still use the printed Rake die.

entries.name: Axe Beak
entries.aliases: Axe Beak / Axebeak. Use the awakened player beast. Keep encounter statistics separate.

source.name: Axe Beak
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition. The rules below use the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The printed Bite deals slashing damage. Cleftbill’s build uses the player conversion as written and carries no hand-dependent gear.

entries.name: Blink Dog
entries.aliases: Blink Dog / Blink Dogs. Use the player creature's own movement. Keep other canid profiles separate.

source.name: Blink Dog
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition. The rules below use the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The player trait block refers to “Blind dogs” in its opening sentence. The title and the rest of the page identify Blink Dog.

Monk Martial Arts allows Dexterity on the Attack action bite. Under p. 7, bonus strikes use the monk die and deal bludgeoning damage. Teleport consumes the same bonus action as Martial Arts, Patient Defense, or Step of the Wind.

entries.name: Bullywug
entries.aliases: Bullywug / Bullywugs. Use Kamstra's player package. Keep Grung and other amphibian folk separate.

source.name: Bullywug
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.version: v2 authored rules text, read in a text mirror
source.heading: Bullywug Traits
sourceDistinctions: The printed traits grant camouflage advantage. The bite and Stealth proficiency mentioned in the design notes do not appear in the trait block. Quib obtains proficiency from the Criminal background.

entries.name: Cattle
entries.aliases: Cattle / Bovine. Keep Cow, Deep Rothe, Ox, Rothe, and Stench Kow together. The separately published Aurochs traits have their own scope.

source.name: Cattle
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Cattle Traits
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
sourceDistinctions: The character uses the Deep Rothe option. All five printed forms are retained, and the Aurochs conversion remains separate.
Dancing lights has material components under 2014 rules. This stat block records the known cantrip without relying on it, since Flintmoss cannot handle those components or a focus.

entries.name: Death Dog
entries.aliases: Death Dog / Death Dogs. Use the two-headed player creature and its printed traits. Hell Hound keeps its own profile.

source.name: Death Dog
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition. The rules below use the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The species traits grant a Bite and the defensive Two Heads trait. The encounter monster’s disease is outside these player traits. A second Bite in this build comes from the Fighter’s Action Surge.

entries.name: Dolphin
entries.aliases: Dolphin / Dolphins. Use the awakened player beast. Its aquatic restrictions belong to this profile.

source.name: Dolphin
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Dolphin Traits
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
sourceDistinctions: Player traits omit the bespoke Hold Breath timer and natural armor from the design discussion. This encounter uses standard breath rules. Charge uses Strength and is separate from choosing Dexterity to make the slam. Finesse lets either score qualify for Sneak Attack with the other conditions met.

entries.name: Elder Brain
entries.aliases: Elder Brain / Elder Brains. It has its own player block. Keep Mind Flayer, Mindwitness, and Neothelid separate.

source.name: Elder Brain
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: pp. 51–52, Elder Brain Traits in the Mind Flayers section
source.provenance: Authored full-text mirror, checked against the DMs Guild preview for the contents and shared rules.
sourceDistinctions: Mind Blast first specifies a 15-ft. cone and then describes the target as in a line. Vellum uses the explicit cone.

Vellum relies on blindsight and has no grasping hands. The build stays below the printed psionic spell unlocks. The profile treats the specifically granted psionics as innate exceptions to the prohibition on ordinary verbal components.

entries.name: Fomorian
entries.aliases: Fomorian / Fomorians. Scope to this player giant and its printed curse abilities.

source.name: Fomorian
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.version: v2 authored rules text, read in a text mirror
source.heading: Fomorian Traits
sourceDistinctions: The v2 block gives no use limit for Evil Eye or its curse and lists no darkvision. The printed twisted-legs speed adjustment says “for 10 ft.” and is read as a 10-ft. reduction.
The curse names successful repeat saves as its end condition and supplies no fixed duration.

entries.name: Fungi
entries.aliases: Fungi / Fungus. Keep Gas Spore, Shrieker, and Violet Fungus in one profile. Myconid and Mycelial have separate rules.

source.name: Fungi
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.version: v2 authored rules text, read in a text mirror
source.heading: Fungi Traits
sourceDistinctions: The three forms share one Fungi profile. Siltcap uses Violet Fungus. The NPC interprets the revival as one day after its own death, from the oldest qualifying kill in the previous day.
Monstrous Races v2 p. 7 uses a monk’s ordinary bludgeoning damage die for Martial Arts and Flurry of Blows bonus attacks, even for a character with a stronger natural strike.

entries.name: Giant Fire Beetle
entries.aliases: Giant Fire Beetle / Fire Beetle in context. Use this awakened player beast and its printed body size. Encounter beetles keep their own records.

source.name: Giant Fire Beetle
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: v2 p. 236, Giant Fire Beetle Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition. The rules below use the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The playable beetle is Small. Its intact glands use the player Illumination radius. No harvested-gland effect was imported from encounter rules.
Wick uses natural armor. Barbarian Unarmored Defense gives the same 15 AC in this build and does not stack with it.

entries.name: Gorgon
entries.aliases: Gorgon / Gorgons. The armored bovine creature is separate from Medusa and cattle profiles.

source.name: Gorgon
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.version: v2 authored rules text, read in a text mirror
source.heading: Gorgon Traits
sourceDistinctions: The visible trait block supplies restraint, one repeat save and concentration. It never assigns petrification on a second failure. Brackplate leaves a creature that fails the stated repeat restrained for the remaining concentration duration. The design commentary also frames the conversion as restraint only.
The v2 trait block grants Strength and Constitution increases and does not give the Gorgon petrification immunity or Trampling Charge.

entries.name: Hell Hound
entries.aliases: Hell Hound / Hellhound. Keep the player fiend separate from Death Dog, Shadow Mastiff, and Yeth Hound.

source.name: Hell Hound
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.version: v2 authored rules text, read in a text mirror
source.heading: Hell Hound Traits
sourceDistinctions: The v2 trait block omits fire resistance even though the design notes discuss it. It uses 6th/11th/16th-level breath increases. Coalwhistle uses the printed traits.

entries.name: Mephit
entries.aliases: Mephit / Mephits. Keep Dust, Ice, Magma, Mud, Smoke, and Steam together under one player profile.

source.name: Mephit
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Mephit Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules. This summary uses the v2 printed player traits.
sourceDistinctions: Dust Death Burst uses ambiguous fall wording. Siftglass treats dropping to 0 HP as the trigger and repeats the blinding save at the end of each affected turn for table timing.
The design notes mention fire vulnerability for Dust but the player trait block omits it. Smoke explicitly lists Aquan and Ignan. Steam has a fire burst despite its name.

entries.name: Modron
entries.aliases: Modron / Modrons. Keep Monodrone, Duodrone, Tridrone, Quadrone, and Pentadrone together. Use the independents described in the player rules.

source.name: Modron
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Modrons Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules. This summary uses the v2 printed player traits.
sourceDistinctions: The player section labels Monodrone and Quadrone together. The play and design discussion is inconsistent on a few forms. Keep the traits as printed.
Pentadrone gas specifies a cone, then refers to a line, and imposes restrained despite its name. This summary takes the opening 15-ft. cone and printed restrained effect.

entries.name: Nightmare
entries.aliases: Nightmare / Nightmares. Scope to the fiendish steed's player package. Keep other equine profiles separate.

source.name: Nightmare
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Nightmare Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules. This summary uses the v2 printed player traits.
sourceDistinctions: The printed player traits give fiery hooves. Fire resistance or immunity, Confer Fire Resistance, and Ethereal Stride from other versions do not appear in the player block.

entries.name: Oni
entries.aliases: Oni / Ogre Mage as an alternate name. Use Kamstra's traits. The encounter shapeshifting and innate spells have their own scope alongside other Ogre profiles.

source.name: Oni
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Oni Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules. This summary uses the v2 printed player traits.
sourceDistinctions: Printed Oni Traits gives flight and Powerful Build but no shapechanging or innate spellcasting. Rusk Toll sources spells from Warlock. Ogre Mage is an alias for the creature.

entries.name: Owlbear
entries.aliases: Owlbear / Owlbears. Use this player conversion and keep encounter stat blocks separate.

source.name: Owlbear
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Owlbear Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules. This summary uses the v2 printed player traits.
sourceDistinctions: Use the class-built Medium owlbear, including its speaking trait, and the printed player-form senses. The player block has no monster Multiattack.

entries.name: Pegasus
entries.aliases: Pegasus / Pegasi. Use the player version. Pegataur and Hippogriff remain separate.

source.name: Pegasus
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceDistinctions: The player traits sit on printed p. 168. P. 169 contains the play advice and design discussion. Use the 40-ft. walk and 50-ft. flight from the traits. Hooves are Strength-based melee weapon attacks for 2014 Rage and Reckless Attack.

entries.name: Piercer
entries.aliases: Piercer / Piercers. Keep its player movement and climbing limits. The related Roper has its own package.

source.name: Piercer
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceDistinctions: Drop specifies a melee weapon attack without giving proficiency. The worked NPC treats Drop as an innate, proficient Strength attack. Its landing treatment follows the printed hit and miss branches, with normal fall prone behavior if the miss deals falling damage.

entries.name: Pseudodragon
entries.aliases: Pseudodragon / Pseudo-dragon. Keep distinct from Faerie Dragon and familiar rules.

source.name: Pseudodragon
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceDistinctions: Explicit finesse clause allows 2014 Sneak Attack. The player sting has no poison effect. Apply v2 pp. 7–8 for the shared Tiny rules.

entries.name: Purple Worm
entries.aliases: Purple Worm / Purple Worms. Use player-scale size and its printed anatomy and attacks. Keep Neothelid separate.

source.name: Purple Worm
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 172 in v2, Purple Worm Traits
source.sourceDistinctions: The Monstrosity line is printed in a different column below the trait heading in the text extraction. The NPC treats blindsight as sight within range for Danger Sense. Add attack and Rage damage modifiers once, to the piercing component of Stinger.

entries.name: Quickling
entries.aliases: Quickling / Quicklings. Use the printed player's speed and defensive feature. Separate from sprites and other tiny fey.

source.name: Quickling
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 62, Quickling Traits, and p. 6, Tiny Creatures
source.provenance: Authored full-text mirror, checked against the DMs Guild preview for the contents and shared rules.
sourceDistinctions: The printed player traits give 60-ft. speed and no darkvision. Design commentary mentions darkvision, which this build omits.
Bram uses a rapier made for a Tiny creature, applying the p. 6 weapon table (ordinary 1d8 becomes 1d2). It retains finesse.

entries.name: Remorhaz
entries.aliases: Remorhaz / Remorhazes. Use this player conversion. The encounter Young Remorhaz stays separate.

source.name: Remorhaz
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceDistinctions: The player traits specify both damage types and no ability-score increase. Apply the ability modifier once to the bite’s piercing damage. The p. 7 monk rule makes the bonus Martial Arts strike ordinary bludgeoning.

entries.name: Roc
entries.aliases: Roc / Rocs. Scope to the player bird's printed size and flight. Keep the encounter roc and other birds separate.

source.name: Roc
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Roc Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra’s DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules, using the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: Use the Medium player body, 50-ft. flight, and talon damage. The encounter roc’s attacks and carry-off mechanic do not supply additional player abilities.
Keen Sight adds 5 to passive Perception for tasks relying on sight under 2014 passive-check rules.

entries.name: Roper
entries.aliases: Roper / Ropers. Scope to its own player trait block. Piercer and Cave Fisher keep separate profiles.

source.name: Roper
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Roper Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra’s DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules, using the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: Grasp uses ordinary grapple size and opposition. Reel contests Athletics only, as specified by this player trait.
The bonus strike uses the ordinary 5-ft. reach because Reel specifies no increased bite reach.

entries.name: Rot Grub
entries.aliases: Rot Grub / Rot Grubs. Use one awakened player creature. A swarm is a separate encounter record.

source.name: Rot Grub
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Rot Grub Traits
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
sourceDistinctions: The authored player trait list has no blindsight. Normal Tiny grapple size limits apply, while Infest provides the specific exception to using a free hand for that grapple.
The design commentary calls the package exceptionally weak and suggests optional boosts. This encounter uses the printed individual creature without a swarm template or added feats.

entries.name: Scarecrow
entries.aliases: Scarecrow / Scarecrows. Use the player construct and its printed terrors. Keep other animated constructs separate.

source.name: Scarecrow
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Scarecrow Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra’s DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules, using the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The trait line’s reference to a stalagmite conflicts with its normal scarecrow appearance. Run it as an ordinary scarecrow.

The language continuation appears before the heading in the mirror’s extracted order. Its reading and writing specify no speech, which agrees with the Playing a Scarecrow text. This build chooses Halfling as the second language.
The supplement’s pp. 7–8 discuss construct recovery and lethal 0 HP for characters immune to unconsciousness.

entries.name: Sea Spawn
entries.aliases: Sea Spawn / Sea-Spawn. Group the printed piscine adaptations as options. Deep Scion is a separate template.

source.name: Sea Spawn
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Authored full-text mirror, checked against the DMs Guild preview for the contents and shared rules.
sourceDistinctions: Piscine Anatomy selects two of three options. Neris has bite and tentacle. His ordinary arm stays available, but the worked build relies on its natural attacks.
The introductory description calls the creature amphibious. The player trait block grants swim speed and omits an Amphibious trait. Neris uses the core breath-holding rule.

entries.name: Shadow Mastiff
entries.aliases: Shadow Mastiff / Shadow Mastiffs. Use its player package. Keep Shadow Mastiff Alpha and other encounter canids separate.

source.name: Shadow Mastiff
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Authored full-text mirror, checked against the DMs Guild preview for the contents and shared rules.
sourceDistinctions: The printed traits grant Shadow Blend and Sunlight Weakness. The design discussion of an AC boost in darkness does not appear in the printed trait block.
Sable Bell is quadrupedal and handless. It uses no hand-held gear or shield, and its build uses unarmored AC.

entries.name: Shield Guardian
entries.aliases: Shield Guardian / Shield Guardians. The printed player guardian has broken its amulet bond. Helmed Horror remains separate.

source.name: Shield Guardian
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Shield Guardian Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra’s DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules, using the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The published character is unbound. The player traits omit the monster’s amulet bond, regeneration, spell storing, and the poison immunity mentioned in design notes.
The NPC’s Dueling style applies to its mace while carrying a shield. Its Shield trait is an independent reaction protecting an adjacent ally.

entries.name: Slaad
entries.aliases: Slaad / Slaadi. Group Red, Blue, Green/Gray/Death, and Tadpole in one profile. Treat Gray and Death as the printed Green progression, with their shared statistics.

source.name: Slaad
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Slaadi Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra’s DMs Guild player conversion for the 2014 fifth-edition rules, using the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The source prints fire bold in the innate spell line. The encounter uses the 2014 fire bolt cantrip.
Green, Gray, and Death share one playable form and can change appearance through the printed progression.
Lichen Mouth uses the Green form’s statistics. The selected NPC has no Red or Blue infection traits.

entries.name: Slithering Tracker
entries.aliases: Slithering Tracker / Slithering Trackers. Keep its own ooze profile separate from Oozefolk and other ooze families.

source.name: Slithering Tracker
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Authored full-text mirror, checked against the DMs Guild preview for the contents and shared rules.
sourceDistinctions: The player trait permits Life Leech grapples despite lack of hands. Size and contest follow the normal grappling rule.

Damage Transfer does not specify rounding or order with other modifiers. For Fenline, halve the incoming damage first, round down using the core default, then apply each recipient’s applicable modifiers to its share.

entries.name: Spawn of Kyuss
entries.aliases: Spawn of Kyuss / Kyuss Spawn. Use the named undead player package. Other undead and encounter versions remain separate.

source.name: Spawn of Kyuss
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceRevision: Printed text mirror of Monstrous Races 2
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published on DMs Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
source.sourceDistinctions: The player worm has no recharge line. A failed save deals 1 piercing immediately. The worm deals 2d6 necrotic at turn end. It has the delayed damage and removal rules in the player block. The encounter-monster spawn effect is absent.

entries.name: Specter
entries.aliases: Specter / Spectre. Keep the player spirit distinct from Banshee, Wraith, and other incorporeal profiles.

source.name: Specter
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild. This profile follows the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The published trait gives a 30-ft. walk. The game advice and design notes discuss a design with no walk, hovering, or inability to speak. Follow the player trait block for speeds and abilities. Sable communicates in writing.
The duplicated Sunlight Sensitivity sentence gives one instance of disadvantage. Life Drain is a damage-only melee spell attack here.

entries.name: Stirge
entries.aliases: Stirge / Stirges. Use the individual player creature and the supplement's Tiny rules. Keep swarms separate.

source.name: Stirge
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild. This profile follows the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: Blood Drain explicitly counts as finesse for Sneak Attack. A later attached drain uses the normal unarmed-strike damage and lacks an attack roll, so it does not apply Sneak Attack.
For encounter tracking, count ongoing attached drain toward the Constitution threshold. The source separates the triggering hit from the start-of-turn drain.

entries.name: Tarrasque
entries.aliases: Tarrasque / Tarrasques. Use Kamstra's player-scale traits. The solo encounter monster has separate rules.

source.name: Tarrasque
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild. This profile follows the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The conversion is Medium and has its own strike, defenses, and spell reflection. The encounter Tarrasque has a separate stat block.
The unarmed hit grants a bonus-action grapple while the same profile bars hand-dependent equipment. This build treats the bite or forelimbs as enough to hold for this specific feature.

entries.name: Trapper
entries.aliases: Trapper / Trappers. Use the monster-derived player creature, separate from the profession, Cloaker, and Animated Object.

source.name: Trapper
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceRevision: Printed text mirror of Monstrous Races 2
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published on DMs Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
source.sourceDistinctions: The trait block gives blindsight 30 ft. The design notes mention darkvision, which this build does not grant. Run Smother as the printed unarmed strike followed by a separate bonus-action grapple on a hit.

entries.name: Unicorn
entries.aliases: Unicorn / Unicorns. Keep the player celestial separate from Ki-rin and other equine creatures.

source.name: Unicorn
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild. This profile follows the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The book calls the innate spell detect good and evil. The 2014 spell list titles it detect evil and good.

Healing Touch and darkvision appear in play advice or design notes without a player feature. This build’s healing comes from Paladin 1. The class action requires touch, which Lark delivers with its horn.
Core unarmed strikes are melee weapon attacks, so a Strength-based horn or hoof strike can trigger Charge.

entries.name: Vargouille
entries.aliases: Vargouille / Vargouilles. Use the flying fiend's traits. Keep Flameskull and Demilich separate.

source.name: Vargouille
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceRevision: Printed text mirror of Monstrous Races 2
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published on DMs Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
source.sourceDistinctions: The ability increase line is blank. The play advice mentions darkvision but the trait block supplies neither the trait nor a range. The action text of Kiss says visible creature within 5 ft. and does not require humanoid or incapacitated; both narrower limits appear in commentary. The NPC rolls against its own Shriek as a table reading of the unqualified creatures in range. Sneak Attack adds piercing for the mixed-type bite in this build.

entries.name: Vegepygmy
entries.aliases: Vegepygmy / Vegepygmies. Keep the standard and Thorny player forms together, with Chief as its printed feat. Fungi and plant ancestry profiles remain separate.

source.name: Vegepygmy
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 73, Vegepygmy Traits; p. 89, Vegepygmy Chief feat
source.sourceRevision: Printed text mirror of Monstrous Races 2
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published on DMs Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
source.sourceDistinctions: The standard and Thorny forms stay in one profile. The optional Vegepygmy Chief feat is on p. 89 and applies to the standard form. The worked Fighter 1 uses the standard form without the feat.

entries.name: Water Weird
entries.aliases: Water Weird / Water Weirds. Keep its printed environmental dependence. Other elementals remain separate.

source.name: Water Weird
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild. This profile follows the v2 text.
sourceDistinctions: The player block gives a walking speed of 30 ft. and no swimming speed. Design commentary instead discusses 0 ft. walking and 50 ft. swimming. This build uses the printed speed and ordinary core swimming costs inside the bound water.
The profile supplies no racial ability adjustments or fire resistance. The build uses a conservative reading of the p. 8 immunity-at-0-HP rule.

entries.name: Will-o’-Wisp
entries.aliases: Will-o’-Wisp / Will-o'-Wisp / Will o' Wisp. Keep the player undead separate from lights, spells, and Wraith.

source.name: Will-o’-Wisp
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Printed v2 player traits read in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: Uses the printed Small size and 40-ft. flight. The block grants no hover or Incorporeal Movement.
The supplement's p. 8 handless somatic and unconsciousness rules apply. Ephemeral prevents the use of material components and carried foci. Shock uses ordinary 5-ft. reach for the worked encounter.

entries.name: Wraith
entries.aliases: Wraith / Wraiths. Use the player incorporeal undead. Specter and any encounter-created servants retain their own scopes.

source.name: Wraith
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Printed v2 player traits read in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The trait box repeats Sunlight Sensitivity. The profile applies it once. Printed Life Drain is a necrotic unarmed attack, with no encounter-monster drain rider. Bereft of Body permits a shield.

entries.name: Wyvern
entries.aliases: Wyvern / Wyverns. Use the player's anatomy and venom. Keep Dragon Turtle, Faerie Dragon, and other draconic entries separate.

source.name: Wyvern
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Printed v2 player traits read in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The printed Stinger rolls piercing and poison. The Strength modifier and Rage apply to the weapon attack once. The portrait uses two walking legs and two winged forelimbs.

entries.name: Xorn
entries.aliases: Xorn / Xorns. Keep the stone traversal and other player traits together. Galeb Duhr and Rockborn stay separate.

source.name: Xorn
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Printed v2 player traits read in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: Each printed eye, arm and leg is represented in the portrait. Fighter's style adds Strength to the second sword. Three Arms withdraws the shield benefit exactly when the bonus attack is used.

entries.name: Xvart
entries.aliases: Xvart / Xvarts. Use the player package. The Warlock of Raxivort reference is class guidance within the same profile.

source.name: Xvart
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.sourceRevision: Printed text mirror of Monstrous Races 2
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published on DMs Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
source.sourceDistinctions: The supplement describes the Warlock of Raxivort as ordinary warlock advancement with suggested invocations and no selected patron. The NPC uses Rogue 1 and keeps the species bonus-action Disengage.

entries.name: Yeth Hound
entries.aliases: Yeth Hound / Yeth Hounds. Scope to the player fey canine with the printed sunlight limits. Keep Hell Hound and Shadow Mastiff separate.

source.name: Yeth Hound
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.heading: Yeth Hound Traits
source.provenance: Player conversion by Tyler Kamstra for 2014 fifth edition, published through Dungeon Masters Guild in Monstrous Races 2.
sourceDistinctions: The printed traits cross from p. 77 to p. 78 at Telepathic Bond. The design notes describe a handless body, which the worked encounter respects.

No armor or held equipment. The encounter treats the hound as nonspeaking, so it uses body language with strangers and same-plane telepathy with its master. The source gives no precise deadline for finding a replacement master.

entries.name: Yeti
entries.aliases: Yeti / Yetis. Use the printed player package. Keep the Abominable Yeti encounter version separate.

source.name: Yeti
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Printed v2 player traits read in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The v2 trait line cuts off before naming an ability for the DC. This encounter uses Constitution, with no damage progression or paralysis imported from elsewhere.
